description.narrative: The Rivers Coalition in Cambodia (RCC) has been progressing since its early formation in 2007 to support farmers and fishers groups, in particular the dam-affected communities, to influence government policies related to water governance of the Mekong byupholdingcommunities’ rights to be consulted on various development initiatives affecting their food security and livelihoods. RCC is a loose network of 28 organizations, consisting of both national and international NGOs, and 12 regional partners. In order to become moreeffective in representing their constituency, the Action will accommodate RCC to define its future strategies and plans by seeking strategic complementarities (clarities on roles and responsibilities) among all RCC’s members. The network is led by its members, while the NGO Forum on Cambodia, a broad advocacy network of more than 80 NGOs in Cambodia, is acting as its secretariat. Funding for the main activities of the RCC is therefore already funded through the NGO-Forum. In view of this project CEPA was selected to be the main actor in this proposal as a key member of the RCC. This is in the understanding that support to an active member of the RCC and with close focus on support to networking activities also the RCC would be strengthened. Additionally CEPA (like other active members as 3SPN, and FACT) is working closely with a range of groups of farmers and fishers, who are target groups for the Action, along the Mekong, Sesan, Srepok and Sekong Rivers as well as the Tonle Sap area.The Action will provide assistance to all members of RCC via CEPA and at the same time strengthen the network to become more effective in organising the fishers and farmers groups.
